scope: Static ROM and device-format audit plus offline extraction from retained B8 capture. No MAME process was run; no production, canonical-ticket, index, log, or TMX file was edited.

fields.byte_0: status/orientation: renderer gates on low two bits; high nibble is separately decoded for device flip flags
fields.byte_4: device attribute byte copied unchanged to device sprite byte 2

render_gate.effect: A status with either low bit set is published; a record with both bits clear is skipped.

phase_clock_owner.operation: Wait until 0x9001 bit 7 is set; increment 0x6059; if the incremented 0x6059 low three bits are zero, increment 0x605A.

separate_dispatch_route_owners.elapsed: 0x3A4C-0x3A78 decrements 0x61B6, reloads 0x3C on wrap, and increments 0x61B7.
separate_dispatch_route_owners.rate_selection: 0x40F8 reads part/difficulty plus 0x61B7 high nibble and writes selected rate code 0x61C3.
separate_dispatch_route_owners.fractional_dispatch: 0x40CC combines 0x61C3 with fractional accumulator 0x61B5 before 0x42BA movement work.
separate_dispatch_route_owners.route_selection: 0x4717 uses 0x61B7 and DIP choice to update 0x61C4-0x61C7; 0x42F4 consumes the selected route fields.

row_inputs.expression: d = max(record[1] - 7, 0); E = min(floor(d / 16), 11); low_y = d & 0x0F.
row_inputs.use: 0x20D2 compares E with zero; E == 0 adds the top-row compensation.

bytecode_branches.condition: If record[4] bit 4 is set, branch to 0x20F7 and publish the base code without row or phase additions.
Otherwise, if record[3] >= 0xD8, branch to 0x20F7 and publish the base code without row or phase additions.
For eligible codes, add 0x0C only when E == 0.
Add by phase 0, 4, 8, 4 for 0x605A & 3 equal to 0, 1, 2, 3.

bytecode_branches.effect: Publish the computed code to device byte 1; copy actor byte 4 unchanged to device byte 2.

actor_renderer.formula: For record[4].bit4 == 0 and record[3] < 0xD8: device_byte1 = (record[3] + (E == 0 ? 0x0C : 0) + [0, 4, 8, 4][0x605A & 3]) mod 256. Both branch exclusions bypass the row compensation and the shared phase expression.
actor_renderer.orientation: 0x2039 shifts actor byte 0 right four times; 0x2079-0x208B use those high-nibble bits to set device flip bits. Facing is not encoded by actor bytes +3/+4.

device_record_format.source: MAME 0.220 official Lady Bug video driver
device_record_format.format: Four-byte device sprite entry. Byte 0 carries enable, size, flip X/Y, and low Y; byte 1 is low sprite code; byte 2 bit 4 is the high sprite-code bit and its low nibble is color; byte 3 is X.
device_record_format.semantic_result: Actor byte 4 bit 4, copied into device byte 2 bit 4, is the sprite-code high bit. It is not an animation-enable flag. The renderer's phase exclusions are a high-code test plus the 0xD8 base-code threshold.

player_ordinary.initialization: 0x032F-0x0339 clears 0x32 bytes from 0x601C through 0x604D. 0x071F-0x0728 writes player record 0x6026 bytes 0-2 as 82 58 56; bytes +3/+4 remain zero.
player_ordinary.live_movement: 0x35FF-0x38xx updates player status/facing and coordinates at 0x6026-0x6028. The B8 raw capture shows 0x6029/0x602A remained 00/00 throughout frames 654-676.
player_ordinary.eligibility: Base 0, attribute 0, so ordinary player publication follows the 0x605A expression.

roaming_enemies.spawn: 0x3062 forms 0x602B + 5*slot. 0x3070-0x3078 initializes bytes 0-2; 0x3080/0x3083 store the selected base code and attribute in +3/+4.

part_1_to_8.part_source: 0x1F26 selects 0x606E, or 0x606F when its selector bit is active.
part_1_to_8.result: All eight table bases are below 0xD8; all attributes have bit 4 clear. These eight part-selected base groups take the same generic 0x605A phase expression.

roaming_enemies.live_movement: 0x407E-0x40C9 gates movement on actor byte 0 bit 1. 0x42BA reaches 0x43D4-0x43EB, which writes actor bytes 0-2 only; it does not write +3/+4.
roaming_enemies.release_status: 0x3A2A clears byte 0 bit 0 and 0x3A2C sets bit 1. Thus 0x81 is renderer-visible but not movement-dispatched; 0x82 is both visible and movement-dispatched. Dormant 0x40 has low two bits clear and is skipped by both gates.
roaming_enemies.independent_den_animation: Existing assets/arcade/enemy_release_reference.json records den animation before and during an active enemy release, while a separate enemy record remains zero. It does not identify the den preview's actor record, base code, or clock owner; it cannot close the den phase gate.

special_and_transition_records.slot_0x6049: 0x3DF1 initializes status 0x82; 0x3E01 writes attribute 0x0F; 0x3E0C/0x3E12/0x3E18 choose base codes 0xE0/0xDC/0xD8. These bases bypass the generic phase. The semantic identity and clock owner remain unproven.

player_slot_transition.writer: 0x596D-0x5996 writes 15 successive little-endian base/attribute pairs to 0x6029/0x602A while setting player status 0x6026=0x81, then clears 0x6026 and jumps to 0x5EF0.
player_slot_transition.renderer_result: The first eight pairs have base >= 0xD8; the final seven have attribute bit 4 set. All bypass 0x605A phase additions.
player_slot_transition.semantic_limit: The sprite-code sequence matches the existing death-animation reference exactly, establishing death-art identity. The sole direct callsite found is an input-gated startup path; its precise gameplay trigger/state role and a current-ROM captured display sequence remain unproven.

source.addressing: z80dasm -g 0 addresses correspond to offsets in the verified 0x0000-0x5FFF main-CPU image. Decoded local spans and bytes below preserve the relevant proof because the generated listing is outside the repository.

input_gate.decode: Read 0x9002 bit 6; the zero branch returns to 0x018C. On the other branch, bounded B-loop control reaches CALL 0x5038 then CALL 0x5020.

entry_and_caller.xref_result: The listing contains one direct CALL 0x5020, at 0x014F. This does not exclude computed/indirect dispatch elsewhere and does not name the input bit's gameplay meaning.

setup_span.bytes: CD 9C 5D CD E5 1B 21 FF 5A 06 0D C5 CD 36 5D EB C1 10 F8 CD 47 5E DD 21 1A 68 DD 36 00 FF 3A DF 5A DD 77 01 21 E0 5A DD 74 02 DD 75 03 DD 36 04 07 DD 36 05 1E DD 36 06 00 FD 21 12 68 FD 36 00 42 FD 36 01 08 FD 36 02 B7 CD 9C 5E DD E5 FD E5 CD C7 1F CD 8F 17 FD E1 DD E1 DD 35 05
setup_span.decode: Initializes the secondary state at 0x681A (including countdown byte +5=30 and progression byte +6=0), initializes actor source 0x6812 as 42 08 B7, copies its first three fields to player 0x6026-0x6028 and zeroes 0x6029-0x602A via 0x5E9C, then begins the VBlank/service loop.

progression_branch.decode: Advances the source actor/progression state; reads IX+6, compares against 15, and branches at 0x5943 to 0x596D when the count is at least 15. Counts 5 and 12 also select distinct source coordinates before continuing the loop.

wait_helper.bytes: C5 CD C7 1F CD 8F 17 C1 10 F6 C9
wait_helper.decode: Each B iteration preserves B, calls VBlank/phase routine 0x1FC7, calls service routine 0x178F, restores B, then DJNZ. One authored table pair is held across 30 service iterations for the first pair, 5 iterations for each subsequent pair, and 65 iterations for the final pair (its regular 5 plus the following 60).

wait_service_and_authored_art.service_effect: Routine 0x178F services the device sprite staging/output arrays in 0x6000-0x6019 and follows device tables/helpers. It does not write the actor record fields 0x6026-0x602A; each transition graphic change is authored by the explicit stores at 0x596F and 0x597D, then serviced by the wait loop.

writer.decode: Sets status 0x81; points HL at pair table 0x599A and C=15; first pair receives 30 service calls. Each following pair receives 5 service calls, because B is reset to 5 before loop-back. After the fifteenth pair, the extra B=60 wait makes the final pair total 65 service calls, then status 0x6026 is cleared and control jumps to 0x5EF0.

table.decode: Fifteen adjacent little-endian words, each stored as base sprite byte then device attribute byte at 0x6029/0x602A.

post_hide.decode: One final VBlank/phase plus service iteration after the actor status is cleared.

graphic_identity.identity_reference: assets/arcade/death_animation_reference.json: shrink_and_wing_frames codes 57-63, codes 82-87, then angel code 88; its reference gives 30 frames per first sprite, 5 per subsequent shrink/wing sprite, and a 30-frame stationary angel before motion.
graphic_identity.comparison_limit: Authored code identity and wait-loop counts are static facts. The scripted final code 88 receives 65 service iterations, while the existing death reference records a 30-frame stationary code-88 hold before motion. The reference is not tied here to the exact current main-CPU ROM hash, and service iterations are not independently proven to equal displayed frames in this transition. Current retained B8 RAM/pixels cover frames 654-676 and contain no frames of this transition. This audit therefore proves neither current-ROM displayed-frame holds nor the precise callsite's gameplay trigger; the code-88 hold difference remains an explicit discriminator.

readiness_effect.BUG-080: Static writer/clock gate is resolved for ordinary player walking and all eight part 1-8 roaming base groups. The direct player transition writes authored death-art sprite codes that bypass the shared walking/roam phase, so it is a distinct scripted presentation path rather than evidence of an omitted ordinary pose-clock family. The exact trigger/role and current-ROM displayed holds remain open. The den preview, special records, later part formulas, and CoCo post-B2 visible timing also remain open.
readiness_effect.BUG-087: The renderer phase counter is separate from elapsed/rate state. No selected-rate-to-pixel conversion is established by this audit.
readiness_effect.remaining_focused_gate: Identify the den preview's record/code/clock owner; confirm the special-path scope; and resolve the exact trigger behind the input-gated transition caller if that affects BUG-080 acceptance. No additional family-by-direction capture matrix is justified for the already-proven ordinary player/roam writer.
readiness_effect.BUG-087_candidate_preapproval_plan_not_e: Only after parent review, source-audit whether a disclosed 0x606E override at the verified 0x407E dispatcher boundary causes unrelated map, HUD, group, loader, or art updates. If isolated, a short window can record forced part, 0x61C3, 0x61B5, elapsed state, actor RAM, and pixels while preserving map/group and sprite-art identity. If not isolated, use the real stage initializer with a forced final-object count only after the source object contract is proven. Natural later-stage handoff remains a separate post-approval risk.
